source.title: Open Source Replication & Commentary on Anthropic's Dictionary Learning Paper

record.file_problem: Whole post and comments are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports an SAE replication on an open-source language model and measurements of its features, extending indirect evidence about feature representations to this model. It does not reproduce the original toy-network experiment.
record.gate_note: The post's measurements of SAE features, their distribution across neurons, and their interpretability bear on V4. Comparisons attributed to Anthropic and results or hypotheses from commenters are not recorded as study results. The post's reconstruction figure is not included, so only its textual summary is recorded.
record.test_reason: The post trains SAEs on the MLP layer of the open-source gelu-1l model. It reports how dense the recovered features are in the neuron basis, how interpretable they are, and how rare features behave. These results bear on V4 (indirect LLM evidence) and in part on V5 (whether SAE latents are canonical units). It does not run toy-model experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author says the core SAE results replicate: a significant fraction of features are interpretable, most are dense in the neuron basis, and the neuron basis remains privileged. Over half the latents form an ultra-low-frequency cluster sharing one encoder direction. The author guesses this reflects something real because it recurs across seeds, but could not interpret it. A decoder-norm bug may affect the results.
record.recipe_differences: A replication of Anthropic's SAE approach on the open-source gelu-1l model, using 16384 features and L1 regularisation of 3e-3. The author reports reinitialising weights for rare features and a decoder-normalisation bug; the post does not give a complete method-by-method comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The rare-feature frequency changed over training checkpoints; constraining weights against the original rare-feature direction led to a new rare-feature cluster in another direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Kurtosis of decoder weights shows the MLP neuron basis is privileged for almost all SAE features, even dense ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP neuron bases are privileged even for features distributed across many neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Median encoder–decoder cosine similarity is 0.5 for non-ultra-low features, with a possible second mode near 0.75.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE detection and representation directions differ under superposition interference.

record.problems: Evidence is from one model; interpretability is assessed anecdotally on the first 8 non-ultra-low-frequency features. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The author reports a decoder-normalisation bug and says the rare-feature cluster remains unexplained.
record.rows_left_out: The post also reports reconstruction loss (92%, compared with zero ablation of the MLP layer; mean ablation gets 25%), encoder-decoder cosine similarity (median 0.5), and null-space measurements. These were not included because they do not directly measure the V4 feature-distribution or feature-recovery outcomes recorded here. Commenter calculations and hypotheses were excluded as not the author's study results.

untested.parts: No toy-model experiments, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Only one 1-layer model's MLP. Interpretability is not assessed rigorously.
Completeness is only via reconstruction loss. Seed stability is not tested for normal features, and canonicity is not compared across SAE sizes.

missing.what: Reconstruction loss recovered: 92% relative to zero-ablating the MLP (mean ablation 25%). It drops only to 91% without the ultra-low features. This bears on SAE completeness and recovery.
missing.locator: Implementation Details; Ultra Low Frequency Features section

record.verdict_notes: Single 1-layer model, anecdotal interpretability, no uncertainty estimates, and a decoder-normalisation bug. The original sources (Toy Models) are not this study, so verdicts are allowed. Commenter analyses (e.g. a cosine-similarity excess among frequent features) are excluded as not the author's results.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network test of superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Tests SAE feature recovery and distribution in one model; does not establish how features are distributed across neurons in LLMs generally.
Does not systematically test SAE features for completeness, stability, or canonical status.
Does not test whether the model's underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Measured how much of each SAE decoder vector's squared weight was explained by the largest neuron weights.
rows.measure: Fraction of SAE features in neuron-basis sparsity categories.
rows.note: The post defines dense as fve_top_10 < 0.35, 1-sparse as fve_top_1 > 0.35 and fve_next_9 < 0.1, and describes the remainder as 10-ish-sparse.

source_check.correct: Among non-ultra-low-frequency features: approximately 92.1% dense, 3.9% 1-sparse, and 4.0% 10-ish-sparse. SAE width 16384; SAE training data 2B tokens.
source_check.locator_found: Exploring Neuron Sparsity, lines 42–44; Implementation Details, line 98.
source_check.problem: The percentages describe the non-ultra-low-frequency subset, not the entire dictionary.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Measured kurtosis of decoder weights in the neuron basis.
rows.measure: Neuron-basis kurtosis as an indicator of whether that basis is privileged.
rows.baseline: Kurtosis of randomly generated normally distributed weights, described as blue in the figure.
rows.value: The neuron basis is privileged for almost all features; no numerical summary stated.
rows.note: The figure is referenced but not included in the supplied text; the qualitative result is stated in the post.
rows.check: Kurtosis shows the neuron basis is privileged. That is a basis-privilege measure, not whether features are spread across neurons or recoverable by an SAE, so it doesn't bear on V4.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the first eight non-ultra-low-frequency SAE features for interpretability.
rows.measure: Number of features judged interpretable by the author.
rows.note: The author describes this as anecdotal and says interpretability was not studied rigorously.
rows.check: 6 of 8 sampled features were interpretable, and the author says the core results replicate. That is the V4 recovery effect in a small anecdotal sample, so 'observed' fits better than 'partial'. The weak sample size belongs in the reason, not the state.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature frequencies in the SAE.
rows.measure: Distribution of SAE feature frequencies and presence of dead features.
rows.value: About 60% of features were ultra-low frequency and about 40% normal; no truly dead features were found.
rows.locator: Ultra Low Frequency Features Are All The Same Feature
rows.note: The author says the ultra-low-frequency features were an uninterpretable cluster; the post contrasts these rates with Anthropic's reported rates, which are not this study's results.
rows.check: Only about 40% of latents are normal-frequency. The about 60% ultra-low cluster was uninterpretable, so recovery is incomplete. That also bears on whether all SAE latents are model units (V5).

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V4 and V5. Approximately 60% ultra-low-frequency features, 40% normal-frequency features; no truly dead features reported; ultra-low-frequency features anecdotally uninterpretable.
source_check.locator_found: Ultra Low Frequency Features Are All The Same Feature, line 64.
source_check.problem: Frequency and unsuccessful interpretation do not establish incomplete recovery under existential V4 or failure of completeness, stability, or canonicity under V5.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Compared encoder vectors for ultra-low-frequency features with their mean direction.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity to the mean encoder direction.
rows.locator: Ultra Low Frequency Features Are All The Same Feature
rows.note: The post reports that decoder vectors for this group do not share the same direction.
rows.check: 97.5% of ultra-low latents share one encoder direction (cos>0.95), so most latents duplicate a single direction rather than being distinct units. This is not a V4 measure of features spread across neurons.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Among ultra-low-frequency features, 97.5% have encoder cosine similarity greater than 0.95 to their mean direction; decoder weights do not share that direction.
source_check.locator_found: Ultra Low Frequency Features Are All The Same Feature, lines 66–72.
source_check.problem: Similar encoder directions alone do not establish that latents are duplicate or noncanonical representation units.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Measured joint firing of ultra-low-frequency features on an input with an extreme projection onto their mean direction.

conditions.value: one data point extreme in the mean direction

rows.measure: Fraction of ultra-low-frequency features firing on the input.
rows.locator: Ultra Low Frequency Features Are All The Same Feature
rows.note: The post does not identify the input in the supplied text.
rows.check: 95% of ultra-low latents fire jointly on one input. This supports that they are redundant rather than distinct features. It is not a V4 measure.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. On one selected input extreme along the mean encoder direction, 95% of ultra-low-frequency features fired.
source_check.locator_found: Ultra Low Frequency Features Are All The Same Feature, line 70.
source_check.problem: Joint activation on one selected input does not establish identical activation functions or failure of canonical units.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Compared the mean ultra-low-frequency encoder directions from autoencoders trained with different random seeds.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between the mean directions.
rows.locator: The encoder direction is consistent across random seeds
rows.note: This is a similarity measurement for the shared rare-feature direction, not a systematic test of stability of all SAE features.
rows.check: The shared rare direction recurs across seeds (cos 0.96). That is stability of one odd direction, not stability of the feature set. The author reads it as possibly a real model property, so its bearing on V5 is ambiguous.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5 as a dictionary-unit claim. Mean rare-feature encoder directions from two random-seed runs have cosine similarity 0.96.
source_check.locator_found: The encoder direction is consistent across random seeds, line 74.
source_check.problem: Repeatability of a group mean direction does not measure the stability or canonicity of individual dictionary units.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Trained another autoencoder while constraining its weights to be orthogonal to the mean ultra-low-frequency direction.

conditions.value: weights constrained against the original mean rare-feature direction

rows.measure: Whether an ultra-low-frequency feature cluster formed.
rows.baseline: Original training produced an ultra-low-frequency cluster.
rows.value: A new ultra-low-frequency cluster formed in a different direction, with significant cosine similarities among its features.
rows.locator: Can we fix ultra-low frequency features?
rows.note: The post does not give a numerical value for the new cluster's cosine similarities.
rows.check: Blocking the direction yields a new rare cluster in a different direction. The cluster therefore depends on training choices, which bears on V5 canonicity rather than V4.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Under an imposed orthogonality constraint, another ultra-low-frequency cluster forms with mutually similar directions different from the original direction; no numerical cosine similarities reported.
source_check.locator_found: Can we fix ultra-low frequency features?, line 88.
source_check.problem: Changing the allowed weight directions does not establish instability or noncanonicity of units under otherwise comparable training.

rows.subject: gelu-1l
rows.operation_detail: Tracked ultra-low-frequency feature density during SAE training.
rows.measure: Frequency of features in the ultra-low-density cluster over training.
rows.baseline: Earlier checkpoints; exact frequency not stated.
rows.value: Around 1.6B tokens, ultra-low-density features started becoming more common; by 2B tokens they were mostly 1e-4.5 to 1e-4.
rows.locator: Phase transition in training for feature sparsity
rows.note: The author says the change appeared late in training and was difficult to distinguish from a constant upward drift.
rows.check: This is the training dynamics of the rare-feature density, an SAE-training property, with no bearing on any version's effect.

relationships.condition: Normal-frequency SAE features in the gelu-1l MLP
relationships.reason: About 92% of decoder features are dense across neurons (r1), and 6 of the first 8 sampled features were interpretable (r3). Features are spread over neurons and recoverable by an SAE.
relationships.display_finding: About 92% of decoder features were dense across neurons, and 6 of the first 8 sampled features were interpretable.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Normal-frequency SAE features in the gelu-1l MLP
source_check.reason: r1 reports predominantly dense decoder vectors in the non-ultra-low-frequency subset; r3 reports interpretable recovered examples.

relationships.condition: Full SAE latent set at the 16384 width in gelu-1l
relationships.reason: About 60% of latents are an ultra-low-frequency, uninterpretable cluster (r4), so recovery covers only about 40% of the dictionary in this setup.
relationships.display_finding: About 60% of the latents fell into an ultra-low-frequency, uninterpretable cluster, leaving roughly 40% of the dictionary outside it.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Full SAE latent set at the 16384 width in gelu-1l
source_check.reason: V4 does not require every dictionary latent to be interpretable. r4 measures frequency and anecdotal interpretability; 40% normal-frequency latents is not a measured 40% recovery rate.

relationships.reason: Most rare latents share one encoder direction and co-fire (r5, r6). Blocking that direction produces a new cluster in another direction (r8). Seed consistency of the direction (r7) leaves its status unclear. Many latents are therefore not distinct canonical units.
relationships.display_finding: Most rare latents shared one encoder direction and co-fired, and blocking that direction produced a new cluster in another direction; the direction's consistency across seeds leaves its status unclear.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: r4–r8 leave canonical unit identity unresolved. Similar encoders and selected-input co-firing coexist with different decoder directions; the shared mean direction repeats across seeds. Constrained training does not demonstrate failure of stability under the original setup.

statements.correction: gelu-1l; 16384-feature SAE; non-ultra-low-frequency subset: approximately 92.1% dense decoder vectors; interpretability: 6 of the first 8 non-ultra-low-frequency features seemed interpretable; anecdotal assessment.
statements.problem: The 92.1% figure omits its restriction to non-ultra-low-frequency features.

statements.correction: Approximately 60% of dictionary latents: frequency below 1e-4 and anecdotally uninterpretable; approximately 40%: normal frequency; dictionary-wide semantic recovery rate unmeasured.
statements.problem: The cluster description is supported, but its limits_scope classification does not follow for existential V4; uninterpretable latents do not negate recoverable examples.

statements.correction: Ultra-low-frequency encoder vectors: 97.5% cosine similarity above 0.95 to their mean; selected input: 95% jointly active; decoder vectors: heterogeneous; constrained training: new rare cluster in another direction; semantic identity and canonicity unresolved.
statements.problem: The gelu-1l measurements are correct, but they do not establish the challenges label or prove that these latents are incorrect, indistinct model units.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Most measured decoder features were dense in the neuron basis, and a small informal sample included interpretable features (r1, r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: A large feature cluster was ultra-low-frequency and described as uninterpretable; its encoder directions were highly aligned and the cluster could reappear in a different direction after an orthogonality constraint (r4-r8).
